A proposal developed from one recorded mistake

In the recorded exchange, an explanation brought ideas from an earlier discussion into a different question. The words fitted together, but the explanation had lost touch with the person speaking.

The interpretation was withdrawn. The next inquiry began with the particular mistake: what had been misunderstood, and what would a more relevant answer do differently?

Read the fuller explanation

One inquiry began when a polished explanation imported an old framework into a different question. It sounded coherent. It had missed the person speaking.

The interpretation was withdrawn. The next inquiry began with the recognition of that failure, then used contrast cases and competing explanations to investigate it.

Where this comes from: When an answer misses the question

Applied epistemology proposal

A proposal developed from one recorded mistake

Studies how an answer missed the speaker’s question. Its suggested checks still need testing in fresh cases.

Read the full source note

From felt mismatch to inspectable structure

The inquiry begins with a recognition that a response missed the point. It develops contrast cases and rival explanations, with prediction on fresh examples as the next test. It does not establish a universal model of tacit knowledge.
